The petitioners have filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the  SCCH17 3 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 injuries sustained by them, in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.10.2018.
2. The petition averments in brief are as under:

On 08.10.2018 at about 11.05 a.m., the petitioner in MVC No. 62042018 was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg. No. KA51ER0345 along with his mother i.e., the petitioner in MVC 62052018, near Anjanapura lake, nice road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA04MJ2767 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed suddenly applied break without giving any indication in the middle of the road, due to which the petitioners who were from coming behind the car dashed to the car.
Due to the impact, both the petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, both petitioners In Mvc 6204/2018: Supreeth H.N vs Shivaswamy H.K on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27625777/
2 were shifted to Sri Sai Ram Hospital, later the petitioner  SCCH17 4 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 in MVC No.62052018 was shifted to Fortis Hospital,
wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

sentences.text: The petitioner in MVC 6204/2018 spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and the petitioner in MVC 6205/2018 has spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
The petitioner in MVC 596/2020 was working in a private company and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.,
The petitioner in MVC 597/2020 was doing tailoring work and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.

Due to the accidental injuries,
the petitioners are not able to continue their work and under complete bed rest and they were suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence the petitioners prays to award  SCCH17 5 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ each with interest,
respectively.
3. After service of notices both the respondents appeared.
But respondent No.1 has not chosen to file written statement.

Respondent No.2 appeared through its advocate and filed objection statement admitting issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reg. 3 subject to terms and conditions of the policy and the driver of the said vehicle was not having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner in MVC 62042018.
There is no negligence on the part of driver of the car.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioners.
The compensation as claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.

Accordingly, respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

sentences.text: Of course, the accused is acquitted from the offence levelled against him, but the standard or proof in the criminal case as well as the claim petition likewise the present one are different.
Hence, the acquittal of the accused in the criminal case is not a ground to decide the claim petition unless the respondent proved that the insured vehicle is not at all involved in the accident.
First respondent do not dispute the accident.
Though second respondent has filed statement of objection to the claim petitions, but second respondent do not enter the witness box to adduce rebuttal evidence.

In the written statement the second respondent has taken up a main defence that the alleged accident occurred solely due to negligence of the rider of the motor cycle i.e., petitioner in MVC 62042018 that means second respondent also do not dispute the accident.

sentences.text: 17. Admittedly, the petitioner hit the insured car from behind.

While the petitioner in MVC 62042018 was riding the bike from behind the insured vehicle, the petitioner ought to have keep proper distance so as to apply break without touching the vehicle which was going ahead.
This fact goes to show that the petitioner Supreeth H.N has violated the Indian Safety Distance Rules and committed the accident.
Therefore, I hold that the said petitioner has also contributed negligence at 50%.
Therefore, I answer issues No.1 in both the petitions, in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 IN MVC NO.6204/2018:

10  18.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, is examined, as PW.5, through him clinical notes and Xray film are marked under Ex.P.22 & 23.
PW.5 deposed that, he examined the petitioner and stated that the petitioner sustained left distal radius fracture and he underwent closed reduction and internal fixation with K wire on 8.10.2018.
Xray shows united distal radius fracture.
The petitioner suffers disability of left arm at 32% and whole disability at 11%.
19. According to the petitioner he is working in a private company and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.

The disability caused to the petitioner affects on his daily activities hence, it is accepted that petitioner is having permanent physical disability at 11%.
 20.
The petitioner has stated that he was earning Rs.25,000/.
But he has not produced any evidence to  SCCH17 17 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 prove his income.

In the absence of proof of income it is to be considered that, the notional income of the deceased is Rs.12,500/ in the year2018, then one day wages would Rs.416/.
 21.
As per discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to Sri Sai Ram hospital for 3 days, after discharge from the hospital there was need of rest at least for 17 days.

So, the petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.16,640/ (20 days X Rs.416/ =
Rs.8320/) with and one attendant at the same rate.

The petitioner has also produced 9 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14, amounting to Rs.75,558/.
These documents are not disputed by the respondents and there is also no reasons to disbelieve the medical bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for medical expenses.
23 . As Ex.12 Adhaar card the date of birth of the petitioner is 14.01.1994.
Accident took place on 08.10.2018.
Hence, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.
24. As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.12,500/ X 12 X 18 X 11% =Rs.2,97,000/ which is the total loss of future income.
25. The petitioner has produced vehicle repair bill as per Ex.P18 for Rs.45,651/. But he has not produced RC card to show his ownership over the vehicle.
Unless the ownership is proved, the petitioner cannot claim compensation for the damage of the vehicle  26.

Hence, I inclined to award the compensation to the petitioner under the following heads:
 SCCH17 19 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,97,000/

ISSUE NO.2 IN MVC NO.62052018  27.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
28 . Though the petitioner has stated that she has sustained grievous injuries, she has not examined the doctor and also not produced disability certificate.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P21, which disclose that she sustained blunt trauma abdomen.
29. Petitioner has stated that she was working as a tailor and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
But she has not produced any document to prove the same.
As per discharge summary available in case sheet the petitioner was admitted to hospital for 7 days.
after discharge from the hospital there was need of rest at least for 23 the petitioner was need of rest at least for a period of 23 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.24,960/ (30 days X Rs.416/ = Rs.12,480/) with and one attendant at the same rate.

13  30.
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17 for Rs.2,29,844/.

Considering the nature of injuries and treatment obtained by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award global compensation of Rs.4,00,000/ as the petitioner has suffered some sort of pain and had to take treatment for her injuries.

31. As already held earlier, the petitioner in MVC NO. 6204/18 has also contributed 50% of negligence for which he is not entitled for the compensation which comes to Rs.2,59,599/ and he is entitle for remaining 50% compensation amounting to Rs.2,59,599/.
32. Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reg.No.KA04MJ2767.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
 33.
The petitioner in MVC No.6204/18 is a victim of the composite negligence, for which she is not liable.
Hence this petitioner is entitle for entire compensation of  SCCH17 22 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 Rs.4,00,000/.

The owner and insurer of the motor cycle In Mvc 6204/2018: Supreeth H.N vs Shivaswamy H.K on 2 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27625777/
14 wherein the petitioner in MVC No. 6205/18 was traveling as a pillion, are not made parties to the claim petition.
For that reason the petitioner can't be suffered.
The respondent No. 2 is entitle to recover Rs.2,00,000/ out of the compensation of the petitioner (As held by the Hon'ble supreme court in the case of Anthony V/s Karvarnan and others).
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3 in both the cases;

34. For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petitions filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner in MVC No.6204/2018 is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,59,599/ SCCH17 23 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 (Rupees Two lakhs fifty nine thousand five hundred ninety nine only)
along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
The petitioner in MVC No.6205/2018 is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,00,000/ (Rupees Four lakhs Only) with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.

The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, thereafter recover Rs.2,00,000/ from the respondent No.1, or if insurance covered,
from the insurer of the two wheeler bearing Reg. No. KA51ER0345, in MVC No. 62052018.
Considering the quantum of the awarded amount, it is ordered to release the entire amount to the both the petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/ in both the petitions.
Draw an award accordingly in both the claim petitions.
Original judgment shall be kept in MVC.No.6204/2018 and copy of the same in MVC No.6205/2018.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The jurisdictional police after completion of investigation have filed charge sheet against Vishal S. who is none other  SCCH17 11 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 than the son of the first respondent, for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
The accused has been acquitted for the offence leveled against him before the learned Judicial Magistrate.
Of course, the accused is acquitted from the offence levelled against him, but the standard or proof in the criminal case as well as the claim petition likewise the present one are different.
Hence, the acquittal of the accused in the criminal case is not a ground to decide the claim petition unless the respondent proved that the insured vehicle is not at all involved in the accident.
First respondent do not dispute the accident.
Though second respondent has filed statement of objection to the claim petitions, but second respondent do not enter the witness box to adduce rebuttal evidence.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Considering the nature of injuries and treatment obtained by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award global compensation of Rs.4,00,000/ as the petitioner has suffered some sort of pain and had to take treatment for her injuries.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reg.No.KA04MJ2767.
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
 33.
The petitioner in MVC No.6204/18 is a victim of the composite negligence, for which she is not liable.
Hence this petitioner is entitle for entire compensation of  SCCH17 22 MVC No. 6204 & 6205/2018 Rs.4,00,000/.
